column2: The fixed-time signal had the lower measured delay at 7 of 8 measured volume points (roundabout: 0, 1 inconclusive); no delay-direction reversal was observed in this sweep. Each point is one random traffic pattern, so a difference here may be chance; only the repeated-seed validation tests that. Delay: signal mean 20.51 s, roundabout mean 29.16 s over 5 random traffic patterns; the difference is statistically supported at alpha = 0.05 (p = 0.0453, Cohen's d = -1.5), with the lower mean at the fixed-time signal. Vehicles served: signal mean 70.0 veh, roundabout mean 65.6 veh over 5 random traffic patterns; not statistically supported at alpha = 0.05 (p = 0.5238, Cohen's d = 0.422): this study cannot distinguish the controls on this metric, which is not the same as showing they are equal. Average queue: signal mean 0.99 veh, roundabout mean 0.39 veh over 5 random traffic patterns; not statistically supported at alpha = 0.05 (p = 0.0596, Cohen's d = 1.4): this study cannot distinguish the controls on this metric, which is not the same as showing they are equal.
